DEFINITION · qeva:1:recurrence@1

Recurrence relation

A relation constraining indexed values using other indexed values, often earlier ones.

editorialdynamics · sequence · computation
Run a related experimentTrace this conceptSearch connections

PLAIN

The idea

A recurrence describes how values are linked across index steps. It need not always determine a unique sequence unless enough initial data and uniqueness conditions are supplied.

EXACT

The compact statement

A recurrence relation for a sequence (a_n) is a relation R(n,a_n,a_{n-1},...,a_{n-k}) that is required to hold for specified n. A recurrence plus initial conditions may determine the sequence.

Example

a_{n+1}=2a_n with a_0=1 gives 1,2,4,8,...

Boundary / caveat

No caveat recorded in this revision.

Assumptions

  • A sequence or family of indexed values is specified.
